rows.gold_value: The Buying Entity assures 100% offtake of the total energy corresponding to the declared capacity except in circumstances of grid unavailability or Force Majeure (no compensation stated for those). If the Buying Entity is unable to offtake for other reasons, it remains liable to pay 100% of the applicable tariff on the total energy corresponding to the declared capacity, provided the BESSD offers the un-requisitioned power at the power exchange (price taker) or to a third party; revenue from such sale after applicable expenditure is first adjusted against the payment due from the Buying Entity, and any gain thereafter is shared 50:50 between Buying Entity and BESSD, settled quarterly. If the BESSD delivers less than requisitioned, only the actual energy discharged is paid.

rows.gold_value: BESSD guarantees minimum monthly system availability of 85%. Shortfall attracts liquidated damages of twice the PPA Tariff for the discharge energy not made available during the month, computed as LD = (A – B) x C x 1000 x D x n x 2 (A guaranteed availability %, B actual availability %, C BESS capacity in MWh, D tariff INR/kWh, n days in month); not applicable in Force Majeure. If the BESS fails to meet 50% of the stipulated availability for a cumulative period of 2 years or more, it is an Event of Default and failure to rectify leads to PPA termination.

If the BESS fails to meet 50% of the stipulated availability for a cumulative period of 2 years or more, it is an Event of Default and failure to rectify leads to PPA termination.
rows.agent_value: Monthly availability below 85%: LD = (guaranteed minus actual monthly availability) x energy capacity in MWh x 1000 x tariff INR/kWh x days in month x 2. Failure to meet minimum 50% of stipulated availability for cumulative 2 years or more is default; unrectified default leads to termination. Excess non-RE charging beyond 49% forfeits payment for equivalent pro-rata discharged energy.

rows.gold_value: (1) Delay in commissioning beyond SCD up to 6 months: total PBG/POI encashed pro-rata, proportionate to balance capacity not commissioned (BESSD may instead pay LD directly; if no response within 7 days or non-payment within 2 business days, PBG encashed). (2) Delay beyond 6 months from SCD: entire PBG/POI encashed, PPA capacity reduced and PPA terminated for un-commissioned capacity. (3) Default in achieving Financial Closure within stipulated time (4 months prior to SCD): PBG/POI encashed and Project removed; after 7 business-day notice without documents or Rs. 1,000/MW/day extension charge, PBG/POI/Surety Bond encashed and PPA terminated. (4) Failure to submit documents, meet eligibility or sign PPA within stipulated time: BG equivalent to EMD amount encashed from EMD or PBG.

rows.gold_value: Under the draft PPA (Art. 10.4) NHPC provides the developer a monthly unconditional, revolving and irrevocable letter of credit, sized at the estimated average monthly billing for the first Contract Year and the average monthly billing of the previous Contract Year thereafter, with a 12-month term renewed annually; the developer may draw on it only after thirty days from the Due Date of an unpaid bill, and NHPC must restore any shortfall within 7 days. NHPC also maintains a Payment Security Fund, for which the developer pays PSM charges of 2 paisa per unit (Rs. 0.02/kWh) as a discount on monthly tariff payments (RfS 3.13, PPA 10.4.9). Back-to-back, the PSA requires the Discom to give NHPC an LC revised annually for 105% of average monthly billing (due date 45 days from bill presentation) and the Discom may provide a Payment Security Fund supporting at least 3 months' billing; no state guarantee is mentioned.

rows.gold_value: Change in Law (PPA Art. 12.1.1) covers the enactment, amendment, modification or repeal of any Indian Law, a change in its interpretation or application by a Governmental Instrumentality or court, imposition of new consents/clearances/permits or new conditions for them, and any statutory change in tax structure or new tax applicable to setting up the project and supply of power after the bid submission date (bid date is the reference date for tax changes); it excludes changes in corporate income tax or withholding tax and regulatory measures by the Appropriate Commission. Relief (Art. 12.2) places the affected party (developer or Buying Entity) in the same financial position, with compensation determined under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021: 21 days' prior notice, computation furnished within 30 days, recovery through monthly tariff adjustment MT=(Y/X) as an annuity over a maximum of 180 months for non-recurring impacts (or until the impact persists for recurring ones), trued up annually, rounded to three decimals, and verified by the Appropriate Commission within sixty days.

rows.gold_value: On termination of the PPA for NHPC/Buying Entity default (after the consultation period and failed novation), NHPC/Buying Entities pay the developer damages equivalent to 24 months, or the balance PPA period if less, of charges for its contracted capacity at the stipulated minimum CUF/Availability, subject to NHPC receiving the amount from the Buying Entity/Discom; STU/CTU connectivity damages are borne by the Discom. If the PSA is terminated or reduced, any termination compensation paid by the Buying Entity is passed on to the developer after deducting NHPC's costs. For developer default by delay beyond SCSD + 6 months, a Generator Event of Default occurs, the PBG is encashed and the PPA for the un-commissioned capacity is terminated; no Termination Compensation is payable on termination for a Natural Force Majeure event beyond 180 days, only undisputed outstanding bills.

rows.gold_value: Under PPA Article 4.9, for grid unavailability beyond 175 hours in a year and for reduced offtake/backdown beyond 175 hours in a year, the buying entity/Discom pays Generation Compensation = (Tariff x RE power (MW) offered but not scheduled by Procurer) x 1000 x number of hours, at the PPA tariff (Article 9, excluding trading margin). The developer must sell the unscheduled power on the power exchange as price taker, and 95% of the amount realised after deducting expenses is adjusted against the compensation monthly; compensation is limited to the difference between actual generation up to declared/contracted capacity and the quantum scheduled, is paid with the energy bill of the month after receipt of REA, and carries no trading margin. The PSA (Art. 2.5) mirrors this and excludes compensation for backdown on grid security, safety or Force Majeure grounds.

rows.gold_value: Two shortfall rules apply, and both damages may be levied in the same Contract Year. (a) Shortfall in 90% availability of contracted capacity during Peak Hours, calculated monthly, for reasons attributable to the RPD/RE-PG: penalty applied to the shortfall in generation corresponding to the availability shortfall. (b) Failure in any Contract Year to supply minimum energy corresponding to the annual CUF within the permissible lower limit of the declared CUF (annual CUF to be maintained within (+)10% / (-)15% of declared value; illustration uses 85% of declared CUF). Penalty for both is equal to one and a half times the tariff for the number of units not supplied (illustrated in Annexure-1A / Schedule 4). Not applicable for Force Majeure or grid non-availability beyond the RPD's control, nor for the part Contract Year immediately after CSD. Continued failure to maintain minimum CUF / minimum availability is an Event of Default: the PPA is liable to be terminated and the RPD/RE-PG must pay damages equal to 24 months (or balance PPA period if less) of tariff for the contracted capacity, recoverable by forfeiture of the bank guarantee/POI.

Force majeure and grid nonavailability beyond developer control excluded. Initial contract year ending March31 exempt. Unauthorized third-party sales while PPA demand unmet incur 1.5 times IEX market rate/kWh for such sale. Failure to maintain minimum CUF/availability can trigger default/termination and 24 months or balance-term tariff damages.

rows.gold_value: (1) Failure of the selected bidder to submit the requisite documents, meet eligibility criteria or execute the PPA within the stipulated time: an amount equal to the EMD is encashed from the EMD or PBG as liquidated damages. (2) Delay in commencement of supply beyond SCSD (up to 6 months from SCSD/extended SCSD): the PBG/POI/Insurance Surety Bond is encashed on a per-day basis proportionate to the capacity not commissioned (e.g. PBG amount x (160/800) x (45/180), month = 30 days), applicable even where 0 MW is commissioned. (3) In addition to other remedies, the PBG/POI can be encashed to recover any damages/dues of the generator under the PPA; recovered amounts are credited to the Payment Security Fund. (4) On RPD/RE-PG Event of Default (failure to maintain minimum CUF/availability, assignment/novation contrary to PPA, repudiation, other uncured breaches), damages equal to 24 months of tariff may be recovered by forfeiture of the bank guarantee/POI. Failure to furnish and maintain the PBG is itself a material breach. PBG is returned after commissioning (within 45 days of SCSD under the PPA) after adjusting delay damages.

rows.gold_value: General Network Access (GNA) is to be obtained by the Buying Entity prior to commissioning/commencement of supply; the Buying Entity bears all transmission charges and losses beyond the Delivery Point up to the drawl point. Additionally, for 36 months from the CfDA Effective Date, up to 75% RE power may be sourced from green market sources/bilateral agreements exclusively for charging the ESS for assured Peak supply during Peak Hours; thereafter up to an additional 50% RE power may be sourced from RE Projects owned by Group Companies of the RPD, exclusively for ESS charging. Excess supply over the 25% limit is not entitled to CfD settlement.

rows.gold_value: Peak Hours are energy scheduling hours between 18:00 Hrs. and 24:00 Hrs. of a Day, provided the selected hours fall within non-solar hours as defined under the GNA Regulations. The RPD chooses, on a day-ahead basis, any 2 hours (120 minutes of time-blocks, not necessarily consecutive) from this window; the 2 hours chosen become the Peak Hours for that day. SECI reserves the right to designate the Peak Hours (including specific time-blocks) during the CfDA term if deemed necessary.

rows.gold_value: The tender frames firmness as 'assured Peak Supply': the RPD must supply 2 MWh per MW Contracted Capacity every day during self-chosen 2 Peak Hours (18:00-24:00, non-solar hours) through Power Exchanges, technology-agnostic, with or without ESS. 100% of annual energy scheduled must be RE power; up to 25% may be sourced from green market/bilateral agreements (ESS discharge counted, not charging energy). ESS charged from non-RE sources does not qualify as RE power. Third-party sale while the daily commitment is unfulfilled is a breach, penalised at 1.5 times (Reference Rate minus Strike Price).

rows.gold_value: For shortfall in peak-hour supply in a Contract Week against the mandated 14 MWh per MW Contracted Capacity, the RPD pays a penalty at 1.5 times the difference between (i) the highest MCP in HPDAM/GDAM/DAM/RTM (or similar collective transaction market) across all Power Exchanges during non-solar hours between 18:00 and 24:00 across all days of the week and (ii) the Strike Price, applied to the shortfall energy. Penalty is levied only on shortfall beyond 10% in a Contract Week; no penalty if the market rate is below the Strike Price; RPD gets no CfD settlement for the shortfall; uncleared volume counts as shortfall; curtailed energy due to transmission constraints is deducted from the requirement. Accrued penalties are recovered monthly.

Penalty is levied only on shortfall beyond 10% in a Contract Week; no penalty if the market rate is below the Strike Price; RPD gets no CfD settlement for the shortfall; uncleared volume counts as shortfall; curtailed energy due to transmission constraints is deducted from the requirement. rows.gold_value: SECI provides the RPD a monthly unconditional, revolving and irrevocable Letter of Credit through a scheduled bank, operative before the Due Date of the first Monthly Bill, with a 12-month term renewed annually, for 110% of the estimated average monthly billing in the first Contract Year and 110% of the average monthly billing of the previous Contract Year thereafter; the RPD may draw on it (max one drawal a month) if SECI fails to pay an undisputed bill by the Due Date, and SECI bears LC costs and restores shortfalls. In addition SECI may set up a payment security fund with a corpus from encashed PBG/POI and, where the RPD opts for it in lieu of PSM charges, a discount of Rs. 0.02/kWh in the monthly billing. The Electricity (Late Payment Surcharge and Related Matters) Rules, 2022 govern PSM operation and supersede inconsistent PPA provisions.

rows.gold_value: Change in Law means events pertaining to the Project occurring after the date 7 days prior to the bid submission deadline, including enactment/amendment/repeal of law leading to cost changes requiring a tariff change, a change in interpretation of law by a competent court, a change in any domestic tax, duty, levy, cess, charge or surcharge, or a change in conditions of an approval or licence; it excludes changes in withholding tax on income/dividends, changes in deviation settlement charges or frequency intervals, and events after SCSD that would not have affected a project commissioned before SCSD. On occurrence, the monthly tariff or charges are adjusted and recovered under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021 to restore the affected party to the same economic position, after 21 days' prior notice, with computation furnished within 30 days and recovery from the next billing cycle; non-recurring impacts are converted to a monthly tariff adjustment MT = Y/X using an annuity formula over up to 180 months at the CERC loan interest rate (or SBI MCLR + 200 bps).

rows.gold_value:
Article 13.4 (p. 67) partially describes compensation relating to termination arising from SECI's Event of Default. The visible provision refers to monthly assured energy during Peak Hours but does not provide the complete compensation formula. Where SECI's default is triggered by a Buying Entity's default, SECI shall recover the specified amount from the Buying Entity.

Where the PPA/PSA is terminated due to an Event of Default by SECI/Buying Entity, damages or charges payable to STU/CTU for plant connectivity shall be borne by SECI/Buying Entity.

Under Article 13.5 (p. 67), termination due to prolonged Force Majeure is at SECI's discretion, subject to Buying Entity consent, without further liability to either Party.

The complete termination compensation provisions for defaults by both parties cannot be established from the available excerpts.
rows.engine_value: Only the tail of Article 13.4 is attached: on termination for SECI Event of Default, the compensation amount is linked to the monthly assured energy to be supplied during Peak Hours, and where SECI's default is triggered by a Buying Entity default, SECI recovers the amount from the Buying Entity; any damages or charges payable to the STU/CTU for connectivity are borne by SECI/Buying Entity. On termination due to prolonged Force Majeure (Article 13.5), SECI may terminate at its discretion with Buying Entity consent and no liability arises for either Party. Compensation payable on RPD default is not on the attached pages.
rows.agent_value: RPD default: applicable delay/supply penalties and, on termination, damages to Buying Entities equal to 24 months or remaining PPA period (lesser) tariff for Contracted Capacity corresponding to minimum monthly assured peak energy; securities may be forfeited; RPD bears connectivity damages. SECI default: after consultation and failed/unacceptable novation, RPD may terminate and require same lesser-of-24-months-or-balance-period charges for contracted assured peak energy; where buyer caused default SECI recovers from buyer; SECI/buyer bears connectivity damages. Prolonged force majeure termination under article 13.5 has no further liability.

rows.gold_value: For grid unavailability (temporary transmission unavailability not attributable to the RPD) beyond 175 hours in a Contract Year, the Buying Entity pays Generation Compensation = Applicable Tariff x RE Power (MW) offered but not scheduled x 1000 x hours of grid unavailability, paid annually, with no claim against SECI. For reduced off-take by the Buying Entity (including non-dispatch under the LPS Rules 2022) beyond 175 hours in a Contract Year, the same formula applies using hours of reduced off-take, paid via the energy bill of the successive month with no trading margin. In both cases the RPD must sell the unscheduled power on the power exchange as a price taker and 95% of the amount realised, after expenses, is adjusted monthly against the compensation; no compensation for backdown due to grid security, equipment/personnel safety or Force Majeure.

rows.gold_value: Shortfall in supply of power during Peak Hours against the mandated energy (4000 kWh per MW Contracted Capacity per day, i.e. up to 400 MWh per 100 MW) attracts a penalty on the energy shortfall calculated as 1.5 x PPA Tariff. Shortfall is calculated monthly (billing month) against the sum of Peak Hours of that month; shortfall is permissible up to 10% below the Buying Entity's energy requirement on a monthly basis and penalty is levied on the average monthly shortfall beyond 10% (illustration in Annexure-F). Separately, any third-party sale while PPA supply commitments remain unfulfilled attracts a penalty @1.5 times the extant market rate/kWh (highest of DAM/G-DAM/RTM rates that day) for the quantum sold, over and above the shortfall penalty.

Persistent failure to maintain minimum monthly assured peak supply in every month of two consecutive Contract Years (excluding first stub year) is default, with minimum supply reduction and lump-sum damages of 24 months or balance PPA period, lesser. Third-party sale while PPA obligations unfulfilled adds 1.5 × highest daily DAM/G-DAM/RTM market rate on diverted energy.

rows.gold_value: (1) Delay in commencement of supply beyond the SCSD/extended SCSD up to 6 months: total PBG encashed on pro-rata basis proportionate to the Contracted Capacity that has not commenced supply (Clause 9.2.c). (2) Delay beyond 6 months from SCSD: Contracted Capacity reduced to commissioned capacity, PPA for balance terminated and PBG corresponding to the un-commissioned capacity encashed pro-rata (Clause 9.2.d). (3) Default in achieving Financial Closure by 6 months prior to SCSD: SECI entitled to encash PBG/POI/Surety Bond and may remove the Project, unless extension charges of INR 100/MW/day + GST are paid; non-compliance after a 7-day notice leads to encashment and possible PPA termination (Clause 21.3). (4) Selected Bidder not submitting documents, not meeting eligibility or not executing PPA in time: BG equivalent to the EMD amount encashed from the EMD or PBG available with SECI (Clause 17.7).

rows.gold_value: Change in Law means events occurring after the date 7 days prior to the bid submission deadline, including enactment, amendment or repeal of any law leading to a change in cost requiring a tariff change, a change in interpretation of law by a competent court, a change in any domestic tax (duty, levy, cess, charge or surcharge) by Central/State/UT government, or a change in conditions of an approval or licence; it excludes changes in withholding tax on income/dividends, changes in deviation settlement charges or frequency intervals, and events after the SCSD/extended SCSD that would not have affected a timely commissioned project. On occurrence, the monthly tariff is adjusted and recovered under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021 to restore the affected party to the same economic position, with 21 days' prior notice, computation within 30 days, recovery from the next billing cycle via an annuity formula MT = Y/X (X = (1/12) x Contracted Capacity MW x 8760 x 10 kWh; interest rate per CERC or SBI MCLR + 200 bps), over a maximum of 180 months for non-recurring impacts or until the impact persists for recurring impacts, rounded to three decimals. The Appropriate Commission verifies and adjusts within 60 days; any decrease in project cost must be passed on to SECI and the Buying Entity, and relief is limited to Project Cost incurred up to commencement of supply or SCSD, in proportion to capacity commissioned.

rows.gold_value: Change in Law means, after the Bid Date, the enactment, amendment, modification or repeal of any Applicable Law, commencement of a law not yet in effect at Bid Date, a final binding change in judicial interpretation, any change in Tax rates with direct effect on the Project or supply of power, or a change in Applicable Permits (other than for Supplier default) that changes cost; changes in withholding tax on income or dividends are excluded. Where the aggregate financial effect exceeds 0.1% of 100% of Tariff payable in any Accounting Year, the monthly tariff is adjusted under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021 to restore the affected party to the same economic position: 21 days' prior notice, computation furnished within 30 days of the event or expiry of the notice (whichever is later), recovery from the next billing cycle as one-time, monthly or per-unit charges in the Monthly Invoice. Non-recurring impacts are converted to a monthly tariff modification MT = Y/X (annuity over up to 180 months at the CERC loan interest rate, or SBI MCLR + 200 bps), trued up annually, rounded to three decimals; the Appropriate Commission verifies and adjusts within 60 days of receiving documents filed within 30 days.

It excludes changes in withholding tax on income/dividends, changes in deviation settlement charges or frequency intervals, and events after the SCSD/extended SCSD that would not have affected a timely-commissioned Project. Compensation is by adjustment of the monthly tariff under the Electricity (Timely Recovery of Costs due to Change in Law) Rules, 2021 to restore the affected party to the same economic position; the affected party gives 21 days' notice, recovery starts from the next billing cycle, non-recurring impacts are annuitised (MT = Y/X) over up to 180 months at the CERC loan interest rate, trued up annually, and the SPD must pass on any cost decrease to SECI for onward transfer to the Buying Entity.
